officialReleaseNotes: Build 254: original English-to-Italian Exercise Laboratory covering every current authoring preset and its supported modes.
title: Temporary Demo: Exercise Laboratory
courseDescription: An English-to-Italian laboratory for trying every current Exercise type and its meaningful authoring options. Five Lessons group Select, Input, Arrange, Match and Presentation; a sixth Lesson is a Story and a seventh holds Assign, which has no preset yet. Inspect or Fork the Course in Course Studio to study how the exercises are authored. Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech to include all listening and pronunciation examples; ordinary lesson progression remains in effect.

content.text: Choose an answer, select a complete set, or fill fixed gaps with reusable options. The Rounds also demonstrate images, characters, reading, dialogue, listening and both translation directions. Listening needs Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech in Audio Settings; Preview ignores those learner switches.
Read the instruction carefully. Single-answer questions check immediately. Multiple-answer questions wait for Check; select every correct option and no distractor.

prompt.text: How do you say ‘thank you’ in Italian?
How do you say ‘the apple’ in Italian?
Which words are Italian colours? Select all correct answers.
Which words name an animal? Select all correct answers.
Which word means ‘yes’? Select the correct answer, then press Check.

content.text: In Fill in the blank, choose one missing expression. In the fixed-sentence exercises, fill each gap; an option can be used again. You can remove, move and swap answers before Check.

prompt.text: Complete both sentences. The same word can be used twice.

rounds.title: Source-language answers, pictures and true or false

content.text: These Select exercises answer in the source language or with pictures: Choose the answer (to source), True or false, Listen and answer (to source), Read and answer (to source), What is in the picture and Listen and pick the image.

How does Anna get to work?

content.text: Type a translation, a missing fragment, a complete word, or a transcription. Accepted answers can include optional wording and alternatives. Accents are preserved; ordinary capitalization, punctuation and spacing are normalized. Only Type the translation and Type the missing word tolerate one omitted or duplicated repeated letter.
Type a natural Italian translation. These examples demonstrate several ways an author can record equivalent answers; the answer notation is never shown as the learner prompt.

prompt.text: The teacher is tired. (The teacher may be a man or a woman.)

content.text: Translate the complete sentence. Several natural word orders may be accepted. Keep accents and apostrophes, and check repeated letters when you type.

prompt.text: I am going to Rome tomorrow.
I study at home in the evening.
Today I buy bread and milk.

exercise.hint: Use the contracted definite article before acqua.

content.text: Type the missing text. Type the missing word gives the first letter as a hint and still expects the complete word. A phrase with pronunciation audio also accepts its complete spoken form.

content.text: Type the translation (to source) takes a source-language translation. Complete the text and Missing letters are typed gaps without and with letters inside words. Name what you see names a picture.

Build an Italian answer from words, phrases, letters or syllables. Ordinary Arrange consumes each block once; repeated words need repeated blocks. Inline Arrange fills fixed gaps with distinct blocks. Word order and Build the translation allow zero, one or two distractors; Image-prompt ordering allows none.
Tap blocks to build the answer. You can remove a chosen block before checking. Repeated words are separate occurrences.

content.text: Flashcards present material without a scored answer. Got it completes a card; Review again schedules it again later in this Round. These six cards cover all meaningful combinations of optional pronunciation, usage and usage translation. A usage translation only appears with a usage sentence. Cards with pronunciation audio follow learner Audio Settings.
Read each card. Try Review again once, then Got it when the card returns. These cards can be studied without audio and do not earn correct-answer base XP.
Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech to include these cards. Play the word or the usage sentence, then choose Got it or Review again.

prompt.text: I drink a glass of water.

content.text: Picture flashcards show a picture with the word; their audio is optional and never makes them audio exercises. Note cards carry a tip or a grammar note.

prompt.text: Use Lei with people you do not know well; tu is for friends, family and children.
il, lo, la, i, gli, le: the article agrees with the noun in gender and number.

content.text: A Story is a Round played in order: a cover, dialogue lines said by the narrator or by a character, and exercises about them (Build 256 Revision 5). Lines are never skipped: without audio the learner reads them. An exercise marked as needing the Story's audio is skipped, like the listening exercises, when Audio Exercises is off. Only the exercises score. The first Story alternates lines and questions; the second shows the line options one by one and has nothing to score.
Read or listen to the story and answer the questions between the lines. Continue moves on; the scroll log keeps the dialogue.

prompt.text: A cup of coffee on a bar counter
Anna walks into a café in Turin and greets the barista.
Anna walks into a café in Turin and greets the barista.
Put Anna's order in order: A coffee, please.

rounds.title: The same morning, line by line

content.text: Each line of this Story shows one option: text after listening, text only, audio only read on request, and audio read aloud although the Story reads on request. Nothing is scored.

prompt.text: A cup of coffee on a bar counter
The same morning, line by line
Anna orders again; every line shows a different option.
Anna orders again; every line shows a different option.

content.text: Assign places items into destinations (Build 256 Revision 7): tap an item, then the group, slot or gap that takes it; Check grades every destination at once. A group may take several items, a slot or a gap takes one; a reusable item stays in the bank. Assign has no preset yet, so these examples are authored in the canonical editor. Picture regions, grid cells and drag placement wait for a later version.
Sort the words into their groups, or fill each slot with the right word. Tap a word, then its destination; Check when every word is placed.

prompt.text: Sort the words: animals or food?
Put the animals in their group and leave the other word out.
Which article goes with each noun?
Which article goes with each noun? An article may serve twice.

content.text: Fill each gap of the sentence with the right word. Tap a word, then the gap; Check when every gap is filled.
